data.name: Physical.Compute.Body
data.value: Game workloads run on dedicated compute nodes rather than alongside the website. Our customised Pterodactyl-based platform decides which node a server lands on and manages it there, so a workload can be deployed, moved or restarted on its own.

data.name: Physical.Memory.Body
data.value: Each server gets its own memory allocation from its plan, isolated from the servers beside it. We watch capacity across the nodes so a busy neighbour never eats into what another customer was given.

data.name: Physical.Storage.Body
data.value: World data sits on storage attached to the machine the server runs on, so saves are read and written locally rather than across a network. Infrastructure backups are kept apart from the servers they came from.

data.name: Physical.Network.Body
data.value: The public website, the game nodes and the services behind them are separated. The components talk to each other over private paths; customers reach only the services that are meant to be reachable.

data.name: Physical.Database.Body
data.value: The panel keeps its state in a central MariaDB service, separate from both the web application and the game nodes. The panel connects to it at deploy time and while it runs, and schema migrations are applied as part of that deployment rather than by hand.

data.name: Physical.Deployment.Body
data.value: The panel ships as a container. A new version is built into a new image, the container is recreated from it, and migrations run as it starts. The same steps every time, and nobody editing the running application to make a change.

data.name: Physical.Allocation.Body
data.value: When a server is created, the panel picks a game node with room and provisions what the plan calls for. The panel is the management layer; the game itself runs on the compute node, not on the web tier.

data.name: Physical.Reliability.Body
data.value: Website, database and game workloads are separate infrastructure roles. Maintenance or an update on one is far less able to take the others with it, and a fault has a smaller place to hide.

data.name: Overview.Compute.Body
data.value: Game servers run on compute nodes, separately from the public website. The Pterodactyl-based control panel manages the workload; the game itself runs on the node.

data.name: Overview.Memory.Hint
data.value: Memory limits set by your plan

data.name: Overview.Memory.Body
data.value: The memory selected in your plan is applied to your server instance. A node's total RAM and the memory allocated to your server are different figures.

data.name: Overview.Storage.Hint
data.value: World data on local NVMe storage

data.name: Overview.Storage.Body
data.value: World files are stored locally on the node running the game. Infrastructure backups are kept separately from the servers they came from.

data.name: Overview.Network.Body
data.value: The website, game nodes and supporting services are separated. Internal components communicate over private paths; players connect to the public game endpoints.

data.name: Overview.Database.Hint
data.value: A separate state store for the panel

data.name: Overview.Database.Body
data.value: The control panel stores its state in a central MariaDB service, separate from the web application and game nodes. Schema migrations are part of the panel deployment process.

data.name: Overview.Deployment.Body
data.value: The control panel is delivered as a container image. Releases recreate the container and apply the required migrations through the deployment process.

data.name: Overview.Allocation.Hint
data.value: A game instance on a compute node

data.name: Overview.Allocation.Body
data.value: When a server is created, the management layer selects a game node and applies the resources from the chosen plan. The game runs there, separately from the website.

data.name: Overview.Reliability.Body
data.value: The website, database and game workloads have separate infrastructure roles. This separation lets maintenance target an individual service without treating the entire platform as one application.
